intent:
Implement GitHub issue #1312: session un-ignore rules in .the-framework/.gitignore should be per-repo globs, not per-user appends.

Background: every new user's daemon re-triggers churn once. Their first session archive appends their email's un-ignore lines to the tracked .the-framework/.gitignore (ensureSessionsIgnored in packages/the-framework/src/sessions.ts around line 78), which dirties their checkout, gets swept into a branch by the next safety commit, and conflicts when two machines do it near each other.

The fix, exactly as scoped in the issue:
1. sessionsGitignore returns static user-agnostic glob rules: "!*/", "!*/sessions/", "!*/sessions/**" (three lines because git never descends into an ignored directory).
2. ensureSessionsIgnored upgrades a recognized per-email file to the glob form once, then never writes again. Unrecognized files stay untouched, exactly as today.
3. The conversations rules (#908) are already user-agnostic: leave them as they are.

Out of scope: untracking the file entirely (that stays with #1298).

Update the existing tests in packages/the-framework/src/ that pin sessionsGitignore/ensureSessionsIgnored behavior and add coverage for the one-time upgrade path. Run the package test suite (cd packages/the-framework && pnpm test) and make it pass (10 daemon.test.ts failures are pre-existing in cloud containers; verify they fail identically on the base commit). Add a changeset in .changeset/ marking '@gemstack/the-framework' as a patch. Push your branch and open a draft pull request whose description starts with "Closes #1312".
